title: The Hollow Protocol
premise: Gideon Crane, sole caretaker of the derelict Meridian Seed Vault, has spent eleven years recording the slow abandonment of Earth's last orbital colony. When the deep-space vessel Anthea returns with a crew mysteriously aged backward, Gideon discovers the reversal was engineered from the vault itself — using the genetic archive he guards. To prevent war between the returning fleet and the colony fleet that never left, Gideon must sustain a fabricated story that the reversal is reversible and shared, while secretly racing to stabilize the process before the de-aging kills everyone aboard. In the end, Gideon sacrifices his own recorded memories — the archive's final key — to make the lie true, binding the two fleets into one people who remember Earth only through him.
about_author: Odile Okonkwo is a former botanist turned novelist who writes science fiction about the people left behind by grand projects. She lives between Lagos and Reykjavik, where she keeps a small seed library of her own.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Dying Light
chapters.summary: Gideon Crane, POV. On the near-empty Meridian colony, Gideon logs the vault's status and the colony's dwindling population, revealing his ritual of recording everything no one will hear. He tends the seed archive like a chapel. The emotional beat is quiet loneliness disguised as duty, establishing his devotion to memory and his fear of being forgotten.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. The final evacuation shuttle departs without him; his name was left off the manifest, whether by error or design. He watches the colony's remaining families leave and chooses to stay with the vault. The beat is abandonment sharpened into resolve — belonging denied, then self-chosen.

chapters.title: A Signal With No Origin
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Years later, an automated distress ping arrives from deep space bearing the vault's own encryption codes — codes only Gideon should know. He investigates the archive and finds access logs he never made. The beat is unease: the past is answering him, and he doesn't like what it knows.

chapters.title: The Anthea Returns
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. The colony ship Anthea, lost forty years ago, docks at the derelict station — its crew children, or eerily young versions of the adults who vanished. Among them is a woman who claims to be Captain Ilsa Voss, aged backward to nineteen. The beat is wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Children of a Lost Voyage
chapters.summary: Ilsa Voss, POV. Ilsa remembers forty years of deep space compressed into a body that hasn't lived them. She describes the reversal event: a light from Earth's direction that unwound them. Her crew is frightened, fracturing, and looking to her. The beat is disorientation and the grief of being young inside an old mind.

chapters.title: What the Vault Keeps
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon traces the reversal signal to a sealed sublevel of the seed vault — an illegal experiment called the Hollow Protocol, run before the evacuations, using the genetic archive to rewind human telomeres. Someone used the vault as a weapon or a gift, remotely. The beat is betrayal by the institution he served.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. The returning fleet's escort ship arrives, demanding answers about the Anthea, while the colony fleet — now a generation ship culture that resents Earth — approaches from the other side. Gideon realizes the truth could ignite war: one side hoarded the reversal, the other was denied it. He begins fabricating a story that the Protocol is stable and will be shared. The beat is a decent man choosing deception for peace.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was a Captain
chapters.summary: Ilsa, POV. Ilsa and Gideon negotiate an uneasy alliance; she agrees to play her old self for the fleets' observers. Privately she confesses she no longer trusts her own memories — some feel edited. The beat is fragile trust and the horror of doubting your own past.

chapters.title: Audience With Ghosts
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. First joint transmission with both fleets. Gideon performs the lie: the Protocol works, reversals will be offered to all. The colony fleet's envoy, a woman named Adaeze who once knew Gideon, sees through him in a single look but says nothing on the record. The beat is the terror and strange thrill of being believed.

chapters.title: Adaeze
chapters.summary: Adaeze, POV. Adaeze, the colony fleet's chief archivist, privately contacts Gideon: she knew him before the evacuations, before he was erased from the manifests. She reveals he was the Protocol's original designer who wiped his own memory as penance. The beat is a devastating reframe — Gideon has been guarding the thing that unmade him.

chapters.title: The Man Who Deleted Himself
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon searches the sublevel and finds his own voice on the original experiment logs, calm and clinical, describing memory excision as a 'necessary kindness.' He cannot feel like that man. The beat is identity collapse: the caretaker was the architect all along.

chapters.title: Reversal Drift
chapters.summary: Ilsa, POV. The Anthea's youngest crew members begin destabilizing — their cells rewinding past their bodies' intended age. The Protocol isn't stable; it's still running, remotely, and it doesn't know when to stop. Ilsa hides the deaths from the fleets. The beat is guilt compounding: the lie is now costing lives.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon and Adaeze strike a bargain: she'll keep his secret if he gives the colony fleet the Protocol's true data. But the returning fleet's intelligence officer, Renk, grows suspicious of the vault's power draw. The beat is a tightening vise — every ally demands a piece of the truth.

chapters.title: Renk's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Renk, POV. Renk reconstructs the energy signatures and concludes the vault is the source of the reversal — and that Gideon is lying about control. He prepares to seize the vault for the returning fleet, believing reversal is Earth's rightful inheritance. The beat is cold ambition that is almost reasonable, making it more dangerous.

chapters.title: The Vault Breach
chapters.summary: Gideon and Ilsa, alternating POV. Renk's marines storm the vault; Ilsa's crew, loyal to Gideon now, hold the corridors in a desperate delaying action. Gideon reaches the core and discovers the Protocol's final failsafe: it can be stopped only by a complete genetic-memory key — a human mind's recorded life, fed into the archive. The beat is sacrifice made visible.

chapters.title: What Memory Costs
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon realizes his eleven years of recordings were never logs — they were the key being built, his life deliberately archived for this moment by the man he used to be. Stopping the Protocol means erasing himself. The beat is the theme made flesh: to give belonging to others, he must surrender the self that remembers.

chapters.title: The Fleet That Watched
chapters.summary: Adaeze, POV. Both fleets converge on Meridian, weapons hot, each believing the other is about to monopolize the reversal. Adaeze broadcasts the truth of the destabilization to both ships — gambling that shared fear beats shared greed. The beat is the lie collapsing and something truer rising in its place.

chapters.title: Hollow Protocol
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Climax. With Renk's forces at the core door and the Anthea's children failing, Gideon initiates the key: his recordings pour into the archive, and his memories begin burning away as the Protocol unwinds. Ilsa holds his hand in the dark of the vault while he forgets her name. The beat is transcendence through loss.

chapters.title: After the Burning
chapters.summary: Ilsa, POV. The Protocol stops; the de-aging halts; the surviving Anthea crew stabilize. Gideon survives but remembers almost nothing — a man hollowed into kindness. Ilsa, who now carries both futures, refuses to let him be discarded. The beat is grief transformed into guardianship.

chapters.title: One People
chapters.summary: Adaeze, POV. The two fleets dock at Meridian, no longer returning and colony but simply present. Adaeze reads Gideon's recordings aloud — now the shared inheritance of both peoples — as the terms of union. The beat is found family at civilizational scale: belonging built from a shared story.

chapters.title: The Gardener Who Forgot
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon, memoryless but gentle, tends the vault's seedlings under Ilsa's watch. He doesn't know why everyone treats him like something precious, but he likes it. When Ilsa tells him he saved them, he says it sounds like something he'd do. The beat is bittersweet peace — identity rebuilt from the love of others.

chapters.title: New Entries
chapters.summary: Ensemble, closing POV rotating through Ilsa, Adaeze, and a child of the Anthea. The colony records its first joint log: seeds planted, names entered into a new manifest that includes everyone — even Gideon, twice, under both his names. The final line is Gideon's own, written in a hand he doesn't recognize: 'I was here, and you stayed.' The beat is memory reborn as belonging.
